$comment: The member-name rule's numbers (issue #3973): the names and depth of a
working set's members. The SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for numbers the API
(Python) and the Worker (Go) must agree on; each side holds its own
constants and a test asserting they equal the values here:
- api:    api/tests/test_member_name.py
- worker: worker/internal/adapters/datatransfer/member_name_limits_test.go,
worker/internal/adapters/regionfsck/member_name_limits_test.go and
worker/internal/application/instancemanager/member_name_limits_test.go
max_directory_depth is the deepest directory level a working set may hold
(inclusive). The root is level 0 and only directories count, so a directory
may have this many components and a file one more. It is the Worker's
snapshot walk, region check and settle scan bound (maxPackDepth,
maxWalkDepth, settleScanMaxDepth).
max_component_bytes is the longest name of one member, in UTF-8 bytes
(inclusive): Linux NAME_MAX, which bounds every name the Worker reads from
disk. The Worker holds no constant for it.
max_path_bytes is the longest member path relative to the working-set root,
in bytes (inclusive): the Worker's snapshot member bound (maxMemberPath,
PATH_MAX-1). It is an upper bound only; issue #3979 decides the final number.
See docs/app/STORAGE.md Section 6.2.
